mainTopic: Defects in the מזבח, a שוחט who skips the knife check, tools for שחיטה, the harvest sickle, and cutting through the windpipe ring
overview: This amud covers several short topics. First the גמרא says a dent big enough to catch a fingernail makes the מזבח unfit. When a ברייתא gives bigger sizes, the גמרא explains that the bigger sizes are for the plaster coating and the fingernail size is for the stone itself. Next, רב הונא and רבא give different punishments for a שוחט who did not show his knife to a חכם. The גמרא explains that they do not argue: one case is a knife found good and the other a knife found damaged. A story follows in which רב אשי checks such a שוחט's knife at רבא בר חיננא's request, finds it fine, and approves it. רבה בר הונא then allows שחיטה with one detached tooth or a detached fingernail. A new משנה brings the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל about a harvest sickle, and רבי יוחנן limits בית הלל's leniency to נבילה impurity only. Finally, a משנה about cutting through the top ring of the windpipe is ruled like רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, but only for the large ring. The challenge to that limit continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How big must a dent in the altar be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what size dent makes the מזבח unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how big is a dent in the altar that makes it unfit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a measuring question: how big must a dent (פגימה) in the מזבח be to count as a real defect? This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא used the fingernail test for checking a knife. Now it asks whether a similar size applies to damage on the מזבח. The question is only about the size of the defect, not about whether a damaged מזבח matters.

keyTerms.meaning: A dent, nick, or chip; a defect
The altar in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: And how much is the dent of the altar?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section; continues the earlier discussion of defects
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The smallest size of dent that makes the מזבח unfit

steps.title: Big enough to catch a fingernail
steps.stepSummary: A dent that catches a fingernail is enough to make the מזבח unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Enough for a fingernail to catch on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that if you run your fingernail along the מזבח and it catches in the dent, the dent is big enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a very small size, the same test used for a knife. So even a tiny dent would count.

keyTerms.meaning: Catches, gets stuck (the nail snags on the dent)

phrases.english: Enough that a fingernail catches in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dent big enough to catch a fingernail

steps.title: A ברייתא gives much bigger sizes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the size is a טפח or a כזית, which is much bigger than a fingernail.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: How big is a dent in the altar? רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says a handbreadth. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says an olive's size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the fingernail answer with a ברייתא that gives much bigger sizes for a dent in the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says a טפח, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says a כזית. Both are far bigger than a fingernail catching. So a tiny dent should not make the מזבח unfit, and this seems to contradict step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: A handbreadth, about the width of four fingers

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
How much is the dent of the altar?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי אוֹמֵר: טֶפַח,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says: a handbreadth,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: כְּזַיִת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says: an olive-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The fingernail size for a dent in the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both opinions in the ברייתא give sizes much bigger than a fingernail, so a tiny dent should not count.

steps.title: Plaster versus stone
steps.stepSummary: The bigger sizes are about the plaster coating. The fingernail size is about the stone itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about the plaster, and that one is about the stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sources do not argue, because they are talking about different parts of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח had a plaster (lime) coating over its stones. Missing plaster counts only if it is a טפח or a כזית. A dent in the stone itself counts even at the size of a fingernail catching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not really clash
Lime plaster, the coating on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: A dent in the stone of the מזבח counts at the fingernail size. Missing plaster counts only at a טפח or a כזית.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two: the BIG sizes go with the plaster, and the SMALL fingernail size goes with the stone.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this is in the plaster,
phrases.notes: "This" means the ברייתא with the bigger sizes.

phrases.english: that is in the stone.
phrases.notes: "That" means the fingernail size from step 2.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּסִידָא, הָא בְּאַבְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources were about the same kind of dent, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about plaster and the fingernail size is about stone, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: רב הונא: a שוחט who skips showing his knife gets נידוי
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a שוחט who did not show his knife to a חכם is put in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A butcher who did not show his knife to a scholar, we put him in excommunication.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new topic. רב הונא gives a punishment for a שוחט who did not bring his knife to a חכם for checking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שוחט was supposed to have a חכם check his knife. Skipping this shows disrespect for the חכם, so רב הונא punishes the שוחט himself with נידוי, a form of banning.

keyTerms.meaning: We put him in שמתא/נידוי, a ban or excommunication

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי טַבָּחָא דְּלָא סָר סַכִּינָא קַמֵּי חָכָם –
phrases.english: This butcher who did not show the knife before a scholar –
we excommunicate him,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הַאי טַבָּחָא דְּלָא סָר סַכִּינָא קַמֵּי חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about showing the knife to a חכם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שוחט who does not show his knife to a חכם is put in נידוי.

steps.title: רבא: remove him and call his meat טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says we remove the שוחט from his job and announce that his meat is טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: We remove him, and we announce about his meat that it is טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different punishment for the same שוחט. He loses his job, and people are told that his meat is not kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא punished the person with נידוי. רבא goes after his job and his meat instead. So it looks like רב הונא and רבא disagree, and the next step will deal with that.

keyTerms.meaning: We remove him from his position

phrases.english: And Rava said: we remove him,
phrases.notes: He means we take away his job as a שוחט.

phrases.english: and we announce about his meat that it is tereifa.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different punishment from רב הונא for the same case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שוחט is removed from his job and his meat is declared טרפה.

steps.title: They do not argue: good knife versus bad knife
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא is talking about a knife that turned out fine. רבא is talking about a knife that turned out damaged.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they do not disagree. Here it is when his knife was found to be good. There it is when his knife was found not good.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב הונא and רבא do not disagree, because each one is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the knife was checked afterward and found fine, the meat is kosher. The שוחט is only punished with נידוי for disrespecting the חכם, which is רב הונא's case. If the knife was found damaged, his meat really is in doubt, so it is declared טרפה and he loses his job, which is רבא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: His knife is good, with no nicks

steps.whatToRemember: Knife found good: נידוי for the disrespect (רב הונא). Knife found damaged: the meat is טרפה and the שוחט is removed (רבא).

phrases.english: And they do not disagree,
here – when his knife was found good,
phrases.notes: "Here" is רב הונא's case, where only נידוי is given.

phrases.english: there – when his knife was not found good.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא פְּלִיגִי, כָּאן – בְּשֶׁנִּמְצֵאת סַכִּינוֹ יָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reconciles the two opinions in steps 5 and 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (knife found good or found damaged)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא and רבא give clashing punishments for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each one is talking about a different result of checking the knife.

steps.title: רבינא: ruin the meat so nobody buys it
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that when the knife is found damaged, the meat is smeared with dung so it cannot be sold even to non-Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Where his knife was found not good, we smear the meat with dung, so that it cannot even be sold to non-Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא adds to רבא's case of a damaged knife. Announcing that the meat is טרפה is not enough, so the meat is actually ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the meat could be sold to non-Jews, it might find its way back to Jewish buyers. Smearing it with dung makes it worthless to anyone, so nobody can sell it at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Dung, the waste in an animal's intestines

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how seriously חז"ל treated a שוחט who skipped checking his knife when the knife really was bad. They made sure the doubtful meat could not reach anyone.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Where his knife was not found good –
one smears it with dung,
phrases.notes: "It" is the meat of the animals he slaughtered.

phrases.english: so that even to gentiles it will not be sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר: הֵיכָא דְּלֹא נִמְצֵאת סַכִּינוֹ יָפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter step to the damaged-knife case from step 7
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the knife is found damaged, the meat is smeared with dung so it cannot be sold even to non-Jews.

steps.title: A שוחט is punished for not showing his knife
steps.stepSummary: A שוחט did not show his knife to רבא בר חיננא, who put him in נידוי, removed him from his job, and announced that his meat was טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a שוחט who did not show his knife to רבא בר חיננא. רבא בר חיננא put him in נידוי, removed him from his job, and announced that his meat was טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story where a rabbi used all the punishments mentioned in the earlier rulings against a שוחט who skipped the knife check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר חיננא did everything at once: the נידוי from רב הונא (Step 5), and the removal and the טרפה announcement from רבא (Step 6). The story shows how strict the response could be. The rest of the story will show it being looked at again.

keyTerms.meaning: He put him in נידוי (a ban)
He removed him from his job

phrases.english: There was a certain slaughterer
who did not show his knife
before רבא בר חיננא.
He put him in נידוי and removed him from his job,
and announced about his meat that it is טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real case that applies the punishments from Steps 5 and 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, a rabbi put a שוחט who skipped the knife check in נידוי, removed him, and declared his meat טרפה.

steps.title: רבא בר חיננא asks the visiting sages to look into the case
steps.stepSummary: When מר זוטרא and רב אשי visited, רבא בר חיננא asked them to look into the שוחט's case, because young children depended on him.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא and רב אשי happened to visit him. He said to them: Let the Rabbis look into this man's case, because small children depend on him.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move. רבא בר חיננא himself asks other sages to take a second look at the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא בר חיננא is worried that his strict punishment is hurting the man's family. So he invites the visitors to check the matter again. This request will matter a lot in Step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Small children (here, the people who depend on him)

phrases.aramaic: אִקְּלַעוּ מָר זוּטְרָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לְגַבֵּיהּ,
phrases.english: מר זוטרא and רב אשי happened to come to him.
He said to them:
Let the Rabbis look into his matter,
since small children depend on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִקְּלַעוּ מָר זוּטְרָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי לְגַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. The judge who gave the punishment now asks for it to be looked at again.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא בר חיננא asked the visiting sages to look into the punished שוחט's case.

steps.title: רב אשי checks the knife and approves it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי checked the knife, found it fine, and declared it kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי checked the שוחט's knife. It turned out to be fine, so he declared it kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי does the check that the שוחט skipped. The knife is fine, so he approves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This matches Step 7. When the knife turns out fine, the harsh steps of removing the שוחט and calling his meat טרפה are not needed. A damaged knife is what calls for those steps.

phrases.english: רב אשי checked his knife,
and it was found to be fine, and he declared it kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the review that was requested in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A knife that is checked afterward and found fine is approved.

steps.title: מר זוטרא worries about the elder's honor
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא asks רב אשי whether he should not be worried about the honor of the elder, רבא בר חיננא.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said to him: Shouldn't you be worried about the honor of the elder?
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא challenges רב אשי. Overturning a ruling by an older rabbi in his own town might shame him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is not about the law of the knife. It is about respect. Reversing an elder's punishment looks like a public insult to him.

phrases.english: מר זוטרא said to him:
Shouldn't the master be worried about the elder?
phrases.notes: He means the elder's honor, since רב אשי just undid his ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what רב אשי did in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's decision to reverse רבא בר חיננא's punishment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Overturning an elder's ruling in his own place insults his honor.

steps.title: We are acting as his messengers
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that they are doing what the elder himself asked of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We are carrying out his own request.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the worry. The elder asked them to look into the case, so doing so is not an insult.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the review was requested in Step 10, the visitors were acting for the elder, as his messengers. Following his own request honors him rather than shaming him.

keyTerms.meaning: Acting for someone else, as his messenger

steps.whatToRemember: רבא בר חיננא asked for the review, so רב אשי could approve the fine knife without insulting him.

phrases.english: He said to him:
We are carrying out his mission.
phrases.notes: He is pointing back to Step 10, where the elder asked them to look into it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מר זוטרא's challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the action as fulfilling the elder's own request
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Reversing the elder's ruling insults him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The elder himself asked for the review, so it honors him.

steps.title: A detached tooth or fingernail may be used for שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר הונא rules that one may do שחיטה with a detached tooth or a detached fingernail, even from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר הונא said: With a detached tooth or a detached fingernail, it is allowed to do שחיטה even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבה בר הונא gives a ruling about what tools may be used for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a tooth or nail that is no longer attached to a body counts as an allowed cutting tool. It is allowed even from the start, not only after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, as the first choice

phrases.english: רבה בר הונא said:
A detached tooth and a detached fingernail:
it is allowed to slaughter with it from the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about tools for שחיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A detached tooth or fingernail may be used for שחיטה from the start.

steps.title: The משנה forbids teeth and fingernails
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה בר הונא from a משנה that excludes teeth and fingernails because they strangle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in a משנה: All may be used except a harvest sickle, a saw, teeth, and a fingernail, because they strangle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר הונא's ruling by quoting a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists teeth and fingernails as tools that may not be used, because they tear instead of cutting cleanly. That looks like a direct clash with permitting a tooth or fingernail.

keyTerms.meaning: A harvest sickle (its edge has teeth)
They strangle, meaning they tear instead of cutting

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
except for a harvest sickle and a saw
and teeth and a fingernail,
because they strangle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר הונא's permission to use a tooth or fingernail
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה explicitly lists teeth and fingernails as forbidden tools.

steps.title: One tooth is allowed; two teeth are not
steps.stepSummary: The tooth problem is solved: רבה בר הונא means one tooth, while the משנה means two teeth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Tooth against tooth is not a problem: this one is about a single tooth, that one is about two teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge about teeth by showing that the two sources are talking about different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With one tooth you get a single cutting edge. With two or more teeth, the gaps between them rip the flesh, and that is the strangling the משנה means. The משנה even says "teeth", in the plural.

phrases.english: Tooth against tooth is not a problem:
this is with one, that is with two.
phrases.notes: רבה בר הונא allows one tooth. The משנה forbids two, since the gap between them tears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the tooth part of the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (one tooth versus two)
steps.terutzMaskana: Only two or more teeth are forbidden, and a single detached tooth is allowed.

steps.title: A detached fingernail is allowed; an attached one is not
steps.stepSummary: The fingernail problem is solved: רבה בר הונא means a detached fingernail, while the משנה means one still attached to the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fingernail against fingernail is not a problem: this one is about a detached fingernail, that one is about an attached fingernail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the fingernail part of the challenge by splitting the cases again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ban covers a fingernail still on the person's hand. רבה בר הונא was only speaking about a detached one, so the two do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached, still connected to the body

steps.whatToRemember: A single detached tooth or a detached fingernail may be used for שחיטה. The משנה only forbids two teeth or a fingernail still on the hand.

phrases.english: Fingernail against fingernail is not a problem:
this is with a detached one, that is with an attached one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the fingernail part of the challenge in Step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only an attached fingernail is forbidden, and a detached one is allowed.

steps.title: משנה: Slaughtering with a harvest sickle
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a dispute about slaughtering with a harvest sickle moved forward. בית שמאי disqualify it and בית הלל validate it. If the teeth were smoothed, everyone treats it like a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters with a harvest sickle, moving it forward, בית שמאי say the שחיטה is invalid and בית הלל say it is valid. If the sickle's teeth were smoothed down, it counts as a regular knife.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It teaches a dispute about using a jagged harvest sickle for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A harvest sickle has slanted teeth. Moved forward, the teeth do not tear the flesh, and this is the case where בית שמאי and בית הלל argue. If the teeth are smoothed away, there is nothing jagged left, so it is just a knife.

keyTerms.meaning: A harvest sickle, a curved blade with jagged teeth

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters with a harvest sickle,
in its forward direction,
phrases.notes: He means moving the sickle the way its teeth point, so the teeth do not rip the flesh.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai deem it invalid,
and Beit Hillel deem it valid.
And if its teeth were smoothed down,
it is like a knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the tooth and fingernail discussion before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Harvest sickle moved forward: בית שמאי invalid, בית הלל valid. A smoothed sickle is like a knife.

steps.title: בית הלל's leniency is only about impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that even בית הלל only validated the sickle so the animal is not impure as a נבילה. Eating it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: when בית הלל called it valid, they only meant it is saved from the טומאה of a נבילה. Eating it is still forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with רבי יוחנן limiting how far בית הלל's leniency goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A properly slaughtered animal has two benefits: it is not impure like a נבילה, and it may be eaten. רבי יוחנן says בית הלל only gave the first benefit here, not the second. So 'valid' in this משנה means 'pure', not 'kosher to eat'.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
To make it pure, free of the טומאה of a carcass
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה, which makes people and things impure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'valid' always means 'you may eat it'. According to רבי יוחנן, here it only means the animal does not carry נבילה impurity.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Even when Beit Hillel deemed it valid,
they deemed it valid only
to make it pure from the impurity of a carcass,
but it is forbidden to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and limits בית הלל's ruling in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל's validation only removes נבילה impurity; eating stays forbidden.

steps.title: רב אשי's proof from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the משנה's wording supports רבי יוחנן. It says 'invalid/valid', not 'forbidden/permitted'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording shows this too. The משנה says 'בית שמאי disqualify and בית הלל validate.' It does not say 'בית שמאי forbid and בית הלל permit.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי tries to support רבי יוחנן from the exact words the משנה chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the argument were about eating, the משנה should have said 'forbid' and 'permit'. Since it used 'disqualify' and 'validate' instead, רב אשי reads it as being about something other than eating, namely impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise: the wording also shows this

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The wording is also precise,
since it teaches: 'Beit Shammai deem it invalid'
'and Beit Hillel deem it valid,'
and it does not teach: 'Beit Shammai forbid'
'and Beit Hillel permit.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that בית הלל only addressed impurity, not eating.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's choice of 'פוסלין/מכשירין' instead of 'אוסרין/מתירין'.

steps.title: Then it should have said 'impure/pure'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: by that logic, if the משנה meant impurity, it should have said 'impure/pure'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But by your reasoning, the משנה should have said 'בית שמאי call it impure and בית הלל call it pure'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב אשי's proof by turning his own logic against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If exact wording matters this much, then a משנה about impurity should use the words 'impure' and 'pure'. It did not, so 'valid/invalid' cannot be pinned to impurity either. The wording proves nothing.

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,
let it teach: 'Beit Shammai deem it impure'
'and Beit Hillel deem it pure'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אשי's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from wording, not רבי יוחנן's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If precise wording mattered, an impurity ruling would say 'impure/pure', so the משנה's words do not point to impurity.

steps.title: These words all mean the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that 'invalid/valid' and 'forbid/permit' are the same idea. Nothing can be learned from the choice of words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'disqualify and validate' and 'forbid and permit' are all one idea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its rejection by explaining that these different words mean the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'פוסלין/מכשירין' and 'אוסרין/מתירין' are interchangeable, the משנה's wording gives no proof either way. רב אשי's support for רבי יוחנן falls away. רבי יוחנן's statement itself is left standing, just without this proof.

keyTerms.meaning: It is one and the same thing

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן limits בית הלל to impurity only. רב אשי's attempt to prove it from the משנה's wording fails, because 'valid/invalid' and 'permit/forbid' mean the same thing.

phrases.english: Rather, 'deem invalid' and 'deem valid'
and 'forbid' and 'permit'
are one and the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of רב אשי's proof.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's wording proves nothing; the terms are interchangeable.

steps.title: משנה: Slaughtering through the top ring of the windpipe
steps.stepSummary: If someone slaughters through the top ring of the windpipe and leaves a thread's width of it all the way around, the שחיטה is valid. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says leaving it around most of the ring is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone slaughters from within the ring and leaves a thread's width of it along its whole surface, his שחיטה is valid. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a thread's width along most of its surface is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It deals with cutting into the ring at the top of the windpipe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא requires a thin strip of the ring to stay whole all the way around. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is more lenient: a strip around most of the ring is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The ring at the top of the windpipe

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who slaughters from within the ring,
phrases.notes: This is the ring of cartilage at the very top of the windpipe.

phrases.english: and left of it a thread's width
along its entire surface,
his slaughter is valid.
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
A thread's width along most of its surface.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a thread's width must remain around the whole ring. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: around most of it is enough.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל both rule like the lenient view of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: the הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a practical ruling on the משנה's dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two major אמוראים agree that we follow the lenient view: leaving a thread's width around most of the ring is enough. The next step will limit where this applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the view of...

phrases.english: GEMARA:
It is Rav and Shmuel who both say:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: The leniency applies only to the large top ring
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל add that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה was only lenient about the big top ring, since it goes all the way around the windpipe. The other rings are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה only said this about the large ring, since it surrounds the whole windpipe. About the other rings, he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל narrow the ruling they just gave, explaining exactly where it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top ring is a full circle around the קנה, so leaving most of it whole still holds the windpipe together. The other rings are not full circles, so this leniency does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The large ring at the top of the windpipe
The other rings of the windpipe

steps.whatToRemember: We follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (most of the ring is enough), but only for the large top ring that fully circles the קנה.

phrases.english: and even Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
said this only about the large ring,
since it surrounds the entire windpipe,
but about the other rings, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לֹא אָמַר אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leniency of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה applies only to the large top ring, not to the other rings.

steps.title: Challenge: Does the leniency really not apply to the other rings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the claim of רב and שמואל that the leniency of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not apply to the other rings. It starts to bring a ברייתא in his name as a challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other rings, is he really not lenient? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the statement that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה was not lenient about the other rings. It is setting up a challenge by starting to quote a ברייתא, and his actual words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 25, רב and שמואל said the leniency of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה works only for the big top ring, because it goes all the way around. The word והתניא signals that a ברייתא is about to contradict that limit. The גמרא is hinting that he also spoke about the other rings.

keyTerms.meaning: Rings: the cartilage rings that make up the windpipe
The other rings: all the windpipe rings below the big top ring
A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה itself

steps.confusionAlert: This is only the opening of the challenge. The words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה that cause the difficulty have not been quoted yet, so do not look for the contradiction here.

phrases.english: And with the other rings, is he not lenient?
phrases.notes: This goes back to Step 25, where רב and שמואל limited the leniency to the big top ring only.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit set in Step 25 that the leniency of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה applies only to the top ring.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement of רב and שמואל that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה was lenient only with the big top ring and not with the other rings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quoting רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה himself seems to apply his ruling to the other rings as well. That would contradict the limit set by רב and שמואל.
